chapter: The Washingtonians, Bechet and drum style
title: Bechet's character and the Salem Willows cab ride
summary: Greer calls Bechet beautiful and tells of a summer job for Charlie Shribman and a costly night cab ride.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: I heard something MR. : You mentioned that I wanted to get clear. Now, you said Mingus created problems in the band because he was temperamental, but what kind of personality did Bechet have, when he was with the band.

Bechet was beautiful. One time we played a gig up for Charlie Schribman in the summertime, we'd go up to Salem Willows for the summer, because the club had closed, and the house -- sort of house band for him, traveled with -- Mal Hallett had the big band and we had

small band. One night Bubber Miley and Bechet and Toby they wanted to go -- I forget where in Massachusetts, it cost $35.00 one way in a cab. Them cats got drunk up there and kept the cab driver. The bill was a hundred and some dollars. They ain't got the money. Kept him up there all night with the whorehouse,kept him up there all night, brought him back so Charlie Schribman had all the big bands up there. He paid, so the cabdriver had such a good time he give Bechet half the money back.
Them cats took him up there, got him drunk and in the whorehouse and everything. Man, it was just one of them things, man.
How long was Bechet in the band?

Bechet played with us, he played at the Cotton Club too. We enlarged the band. Toby, Bechet, Johnny Hodges, Carney, he stayed with us so then he wanted to go to Europe so he went to Europe and stayed.
But he got along well with everybody in the band?
